questions.scenario: An insurance application lets customers upload a photo of vehicle damage. The application must ask a model deployed in Microsoft Foundry to describe the visible damage.
questions.question: Which type of model deployment is required?

options.text: A multimodal model that accepts image input, such as GPT-4.1
options.why: Correct. Multimodal models can interpret images included in a prompt.
Embedding models return vectors and do not describe images in natural language.
A text-only model cannot interpret images.
Speech-to-text models transcribe audio.

questions.explanation: Interpreting visual input in a prompt requires a multimodal model that supports image input.

questions.question: You send an image to a multimodal model by using an input_image content part in the Responses API. Which TWO formats can you use for the image?

options.why: Correct. The service can fetch an image from an https URL.
Correct. A data URL such as data:image/jpeg;base64,... embeds the image in the request.

options.text: A local file path such as C:\images\car.jpg
options.why: The service cannot read files on your computer.
SSML controls speech synthesis and is not an image format.

questions.explanation: input_image accepts an https URL or a base64 data URL.

questions.question: You want to test whether a multimodal model can read labels in product photos before you write any code. What should you use?

options.text: The chat playground in the Microsoft Foundry portal with an attached image
options.why: Correct. The chat playground lets you attach images to prompts without code.
The pricing calculator estimates costs.
Azure Policy enforces resource rules.
Batch transcription processes audio files.

questions.explanation: The chat playground supports image attachments for testing multimodal deployments.

questions.question: A multimodal model repeatedly miscounts small items in shelf photos. Which action is most likely to improve the results?

options.text: Send a clearer, cropped image and ask a narrower, specific question
options.why: Correct. Clear images and specific prompts reduce misreads.
Higher temperature increases randomness and does not improve accuracy.
A system message helps guide the response. Removing it does not improve counting.

options.text: Convert the image to an audio file
options.why: Audio input does not help a model interpret an image.

questions.explanation: Image quality and prompt specificity strongly affect how accurately a multimodal model interprets visual details. Exact counts should still be verified.

questions.question: Which statement about image inputs to a model deployment in Microsoft Foundry is true?

options.text: Content filters configured on the deployment also evaluate image inputs.
options.why: Correct. Guardrails apply to images as well as text.
Images are converted to tokens, and larger or higher-detail images use more.

options.text: A single message can contain only one image.
options.why: A message can contain several images, for example to compare them.

options.text: Image inputs are used to retrain the foundation model.
options.why: Customer prompts and completions are not used to train the foundation models.

questions.explanation: Guardrails evaluate image inputs, images consume tokens, and several images can be sent in one message.
